body: Tenchu Z is K2's Xbox 360 stealth-action game, first released in Japan as Tenchu Senran on 5 October 2006. The player creates a new recruit of the Azuma Ninja Clan rather than selecting an established hero. Rikimaru gives assignments as Lord Gohda's domain approaches conflict with neighbouring Ogawara. Assassinations, rescues and the recovery of stolen objects provide different objectives within fifty missions. The created ninja develops through that work, connecting the series' quiet approaches and sudden attacks to a character whose appearance and abilities belong to the player's own campaign.

Strength, agility and health can be adjusted, while gold earned through strong performances buys abilities, items and new visual options. Special attacks and editable combinations provide further ways to shape the character. Preparation therefore reaches beyond choosing the next destination. The player develops a ninja suited to a preferred approach, then has to make those choices work within the mission's objectives and patrols. The relationship between stealth and reward gives an efficient assignment continuing value, as the resources earned can improve the equipment and skills available when the next infiltration begins.

Four-player cooperative play through Xbox Live allows several created ninjas to undertake missions together. That changes the familiar solitary infiltration into something whose approaches can be shared, with each participant bringing a developed character to the assignment. Kiyoji Tomita directed the game, published internationally by Microsoft in 2007. Returning figures such as Rikimaru maintain the link to earlier Tenchu adventures, while the custom protagonist and cooperative structure distinguish this entry. Tenchu Z's central shift is to make the role of ninja an identity built through repeated work rather than one inherited entirely from a predetermined hero.
